candidate: exact Fourier support bound plus approximate fixed-atom covering bound for positive Pfaffian sign quadrature

target_scope.matrix_domain: real rational matrices, a subclass of rational-complex inputs
target_scope.sector: supplied full half-sector k=n/2 with n even
target_scope.weights: nonnegative rational entries in the explicit block-pair test family
target_scope.oracle_output: scalar Z only; the theorem concerns a separate literal Pfaffian-evaluation quadrature class

claims.statement: For any pairing pi of n sites and positive rational a_i,b_i, the block-pair matrix A_pi satisfies Z_{n/2}(A_pi)=product_i(a_i^2+b_i^2).
On the same family, the normalized Pfaffian-square integrand equals product_i(1-gamma_i sigma_{u_i}sigma_{v_i}), where gamma_i=2a_i b_i/(a_i^2+b_i^2), and its uniform sign mean is one.
An input-independent exact quadrature for every rational block-pair instance has zero Fourier moment at every nonempty even subset of sign coordinates.
Every normalized exact sign quadrature in the stated class has at least 2^(n-1) atoms; uniform representatives of global-sign classes attain this bound.

Any input-independent finite sign-atom support whose input-dependent nonnegative Pfaffian-square weights relatively approximate every rational block-pair instance with error epsilon<1 must have at least ceil(binomial(2k,k)/2^k) atoms.

cost_scope.per_atom_pfaffian_evaluation: polynomial bit cost in explicit rational input length
cost_scope.error_failure_transfer: relative support theorem assumes deterministic error epsilon<1; no randomized failure-probability result is claimed

source_status.Pfaffian_minor_summation: prior framework, cited; special family identity is directly derived
source_status.linear_matroid_parity: prior support interpretation, not a weighted counting result

nonclaims: No lower bound for arbitrary Z_k algorithms or FPRASs.
The approximation theorem does not rule out input-dependent or randomized sign sampling; it requires one fixed atom support shared by every input.
No obstruction to adaptive methods or implicitly aggregated sign formulas.
No PM open-problem consequence; OA113 plus PC-05 remains the conditional baseline recorded in cycle2.
No claim that the explicit block-pair family is computationally hard; its Z value has a direct product formula.
No claim against all positive matching, mixed-discriminant, determinantal, or tensor-network lifts.
